glossary.gloss: A lightweight container on a Proxmox server — a small, isolated box that runs one service, sharing the host's brain.
Free software that turns one physical computer into many virtual ones, so each service gets its own isolated space.
A private network that connects your own devices over the internet, encrypted, as if they were on one home Wi-Fi.
The service that creates and manages a tailnet (that private device-to-device network).
A fast, modern VPN technology — a backup way for devices to reach each other if the main network path fails.
A private, encrypted tunnel between devices or networks.
Software that serves AI models efficiently so many requests can be answered at once.
A traffic controller for AI models — one address in front of many model providers, with automatic failover.
A tool for running AI models on your own machines or through a hosted plan.
The graphics chip in a computer — also the part that does most of the math when an AI model thinks.
The moment an AI model produces an answer.
Mixture of Experts — a type of AI model that only switches on a small part of itself for each question, which saves computing power.
A standardized test that scores how well an AI model fixes real software bugs.
A standardized test of graduate-level science questions for AI models.
Model Context Protocol — a standard way for AI agents to connect to external tools and data.
A scheduler that runs a job at set times — the Alarm Clock of a server.
A small recurring check that stays silent when everything is healthy and raises an alert when something fails.
A background program that runs continuously, like a service.
The service manager on Linux servers — it starts programs at boot and keeps them running.
A secure, text-based way to log into another computer over the network.
Software that packs an app with everything it needs into an isolated 'container' so it runs the same everywhere.
An isolated test environment — if the agent breaks something inside it, nothing outside is touched.
A modern way to describe colors numerically so contrast and accessibility can be measured precisely.
Web Content Accessibility Guidelines — the shared rulebook for making websites usable by everyone, including contrast minimums.
A machine-readable description of a page's content, added so search engines understand it.
A feed format that lets readers subscribe to new posts without visiting the site.
Page tags that decide what a link looks like when shared on social media.
A one-time sign-in link emailed to you — no password needed.
The standard 'Sign in with…' flow that lets one service confirm your identity without seeing your password.
Numeric descriptions of images that let software find pictures by meaning, not by filename.
A video export where the same input always produces the exact same output — no re-editing by hand.
A task board with columns like to-do / doing / done.
The small program that picks tasks off the board and hands them to the right agent.
The author's home network of small servers and agents working as one system.
The site's name for a long-form essay — a numbered entry in the field log.
The site's name for a video episode — the on-camera twin of an essay.
Proof that a claim is real: a link to the repo, runbook, screenshot, or result behind it.
An isolated agent setup — its own model, tools, memory, and settings.
A usage limit or allowance on an AI service.
Software designed so your data and computing stay on your own machines first, the cloud second.
Run on your own hardware instead of a rented cloud service.
Software whose code is public — anyone can inspect, use, and change it.
The instructions or question you give an AI model.
How much text an AI model can consider at once — its working memory.
The small chunks of text (roughly word pieces) that AI models read and write; usage is billed in tokens.
A defined way for programs to talk to each other over the network.
One specific address of an API — one 'door' a program can call.
Put new code or content live on a server.
A stored copy of data or files so repeat requests are faster.
The waiting time between a request and its answer.
How many requests a system can handle per second.
A backup path that takes over automatically when the primary one fails.
Handing a problem up to a stronger model — or to a human — when the first attempt can't solve it.
Produce the final video, image, or page from source files.
Convert media into a standard file format.
a task that runs on a schedule
a private, versioned library of notes and files
a plug-in tool an agent can call
a step-by-step guide
a file that saves work in progress
a simple file database
rules for readable contrast
the AI models behind chatbots
a go-between: one address in, many models behind it
the service's 'too many requests' reply
switching to a backup automatically
A computer program that does tasks on its own - reading, writing, and running commands - while following written instructions.
A helper agent that clears bulk background work in one pass: log cleanups, searches, summaries.
A short video cut from a longer one. Spelled CLIP, it also names a tool that finds images by meaning.
